inputs.layout:
# tally in Go: the layout

A layout of tally.fabulac.cosm for its transconception into Go: the files of the program to be, in the order they are written, what each holds, and the name each kept interface takes there. Written from the fabulac alone.

## Files, in the order they are written

| # | file | holds |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | go.mod | the Go package |
| 2 | main.go | the whole program |

## Interfaces

| interface | file | name |
|---|---|---|
| C:interface/command.tally | main.go | N_command_tally |
| C:interface/command.add | main.go | N_command_add |
| C:interface/command.show | main.go | N_command_show |
| C:interface/command.undo | main.go | N_command_undo |
| C:interface/tally.cli.main | main.go | N_tally_cli_main |
| C:interface/tally.ledger.ledger_path | main.go | N_tally_ledger_ledger_path |
| C:interface/tally.ledger.read | main.go | N_tally_ledger_read |
| C:interface/tally.ledger.add | main.go | N_tally_ledger_add |
| C:interface/tally.ledger.undo | main.go | N_tally_ledger_undo |
| C:interface/tally.ledger.totals | main.go | N_tally_ledger_totals |
| C:interface/tally.ledger.LedgerError | main.go | N_tally_ledger_LedgerError |
| C:interface/tally.render.rows | main.go | N_tally_render_rows |
| C:interface/tally.render.empty_message | main.go | N_tally_render_empty_message |
| C:interface/format.ledger-line | main.go | N_format_ledger_line |

## Gaps, and what fills each

| gap | fill |
|---|---|
| C:reliance/argparse-surface | written in main.go |

file: {path: main.go, holds: the whole program}
interfaces:
- id: C:interface/command.tally
  name: tally
  summary: The program, with three subcommands and --version; a subcommand is required.
  surface: command
  signature: tally [-h] [--version] {add,show,undo} ...
  takes:
  - {name: --version, means: print "tally 0.2.0" and exit 0}
  - {name: command, required: true, means: 'add, show or undo'}
  gives: {exit: 0 done; 1 a ledger error (message on standard error); 2 a usage error (argparse's message)}
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  takes the name: N_command_tally
- id: C:interface/command.add
  name: tally add
  summary: Adds N to the count called NAME and prints the new total.
  surface: command
  signature: tally add [-h] name [n]
  takes:
  - {name: name, type: str, required: true, means: 'one word, no spaces'}
  - {name: n, type: int, default: 1, means: what to add; may be negative (tally add pages -2); never 0}
  gives: {output: 'NAME: TOTAL', exit: 0}
  raises:
  - {error: LedgerError, when: the name is empty or holds a space, message: 'tally: a name is one word, with no spaces'}
  - {error: LedgerError, when: n is 0, message: 'tally: adding 0 changes nothing'}
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  takes the name: N_command_add
- id: C:interface/command.show
  name: tally show
  summary: Prints every total, as rows with bars or as one JSON object.
  surface: command
  signature: tally show [-h] [--all] [--json]
  takes:
  - {name: --all, type: flag, means: include totals of 0}
  - {name: --json, type: flag, means: 'print one JSON object, keys sorted, instead of rows'}
  gives: {output: 'the rows of tally.render.rows, or its empty message; with --json, one JSON object', exit: 0}
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  takes the name: N_command_show
- id: C:interface/command.undo
  name: tally undo
  summary: Cancels the latest add that has not been undone, and says what it did.
  surface: command
  signature: tally undo [-h]
  gives: {output: 'undid <the cancelled delta, signed> on NAME; NAME: TOTAL, or nothing to undo', exit: 0}
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  takes the name: N_command_undo
- id: C:interface/tally.cli.main
  name: main
  summary: Runs the command line on argv and returns the exit status; the ledger is the one ledger_path() names.
  surface: function
  signature: 'def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int'
  takes:
  - {name: argv, type: 'list[str] | None', default: None, means: the arguments after the program name; None reads sys.argv}
  gives: {type: int, means: '0, or 1 after a LedgerError; argparse exits with 2 itself on a usage error'}
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  takes the name: N_tally_cli_main
- id: C:interface/tally.ledger.ledger_path
  name: ledger_path
  summary: The ledger's path, from the environment or the default in the home folder.
  surface: function
  signature: 'def ledger_path(env: dict | None = None) -> Path'
  takes:
  - {name: env, type: dict | None, default: None, means: the environment to read; None reads os.environ}
  gives: {type: Path, means: 'TALLY_FILE stripped and with ~ expanded when it is set and not blank, else Path.home() / ".tally.jsonl"'}
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  takes the name: N_tally_ledger_ledger_path
- id: C:interface/tally.ledger.read
  name: read
  summary: Every entry of a ledger, in the order written.
  surface: function
  signature: 'def read(path: Path) -> list[Entry]'
  takes:
  - {name: path, type: Path}
  gives: {type: 'list[Entry]', means: an empty list when the file does not exist}
  raises:
  - {error: LedgerError, when: 'a non-blank line is not a JSON object with at, name and delta', message: '<path>: line <n> is not a tally entry'}
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  takes the name: N_tally_ledger_read
- id: C:interface/tally.ledger.add
  name: add
  summary: Appends one count to the ledger and returns the entry written.
  surface: function
  signature: 'def add(path: Path, name: str, delta: int = 1, now: float | None = None) -> Entry'
  takes:
  - {name: path, type: Path}
  - {name: name, type: str, means: stripped of surrounding space before it is checked}
  - {name: delta, type: int, default: 1}
  - {name: now, type: float | None, default: None, means: the entry's time; None is time.time()}
  gives: {type: Entry}
  raises:
  - {error: LedgerError, when: the stripped name is empty or holds any whitespace, message: 'a name is one word, with no spaces'}
  - {error: LedgerError, when: delta is 0, message: adding 0 changes nothing}
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  takes the name: N_tally_ledger_add
- id: C:interface/tally.ledger.undo
  name: undo
  summary: Cancels the latest entry that can be cancelled, by appending its opposite; returns that new entry or None.
  surface: function
  signature: 'def undo(path: Path, now: float | None = None) -> Entry | None'
  takes:
  - {name: path, type: Path}
  - {name: now, type: float | None, default: None}
  gives: {type: Entry | None, means: 'the entry appended, or None when nothing is left to undo'}
  raises:
  - {error: LedgerError, when: read raises}
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  takes the name: N_tally_ledger_undo
- id: C:interface/tally.ledger.totals
  name: totals
  summary: Each name's total, names in alphabetical order.
  surface: function
  signature: 'def totals(entries: list[Entry]) -> dict[str, int]'
  takes:
  - {name: entries, type: 'list[Entry]'}
  gives: {type: 'dict[str, int]', means: 'every name that appears, totals of 0 included, keys sorted'}
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  takes the name: N_tally_ledger_totals
- id: C:interface/tally.ledger.LedgerError
  name: LedgerError
  summary: The one error tally raises on purpose; its message is shown to the user as it is.
  surface: class
  signature: class LedgerError(Exception)
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  takes the name: N_tally_ledger_LedgerError
- id: C:interface/tally.render.rows
  name: rows
  summary: The lines that draw a set of totals, one per name.
  surface: function
  signature: 'def rows(totals: dict[str, int], show_all: bool = False) -> list[str]'
  takes:
  - {name: totals, type: 'dict[str, int]', means: in the order to draw them}
  - {name: show_all, type: bool, default: false, means: include totals of 0}
  gives: {type: 'list[str]', means: one line per name shown; an empty list when none is shown}
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  takes the name: N_tally_render_rows
- id: C:interface/tally.render.empty_message
  name: empty_message
  summary: What show prints when it has no rows.
  surface: function
  signature: 'def empty_message(show_all: bool) -> str'
  gives: {type: str, means: '"nothing tallied yet" with --all; without it, "nothing tallied yet (or every total is 0; try --all)"'}
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  takes the name: N_tally_render_empty_message
- id: C:interface/format.ledger-line
  name: a ledger line
  summary: The ledger's format, one JSON object per line, which another program may read or append to.
  surface: format
  signature: '{"at": <float seconds>, "delta": <int>, "name": <str>, ["undoes": <int, a line number from 1>]} with keys sorted, one per line, UTF-8, LF'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  takes the name: N_format_ledger_line
about them:
- id: C:behaviour/add
  name: An add appends and reports
  summary: tally add checks the name and the number, appends one line to the ledger, then reads the whole ledger back and prints the name's new total.
  does: 'Strips NAME; refuses an empty name, a name with whitespace, or N of 0; creates the ledger''s folder if needed; appends {"at", "delta", "name"}; prints NAME: TOTAL.'
  when: tally add NAME [N]
  edges:
  - {given: tally add pages -2, then: 'a negative N is read as the number, not an option; pages goes down by 2'}
  - {given: a ledger that does not exist yet, then: 'it is created, with its parent folders'}
  errors:
  - {when: tally add "two words", message: 'tally: a name is one word, with no spaces', exit: 1}
  - {when: tally add tea 0, message: 'tally: adding 0 changes nothing', exit: 1}
  - {when: tally add with no name, message: argparse's usage and its 'the following arguments are required' line, exit: 2}
  of: ['C:interface/command.add', 'C:interface/tally.ledger.add']
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
- id: C:behaviour/undo
  name: Undo walks back
  summary: tally undo looks back from the newest line for an add that is neither an undo nor already undone, and appends its opposite naming its line.
  does: 'Reads every entry; collects the line numbers that undo entries name; from the last entry to the first, takes the first that has no undoes and is not named; appends {name, delta: -delta, undoes: its line}; prints "undid D on NAME; NAME: TOTAL", D being the cancelled entry''s delta with its sign (undid +1, undid -2).'
  when: tally undo
  edges:
  - {given: undo after undo, then: the second cancels the add before the first's; an undo is never itself undone}
  - {given: 'every add already undone, or an empty ledger', then: 'prints "nothing to undo", writes nothing, exit 0'}
  of: ['C:interface/command.undo', 'C:interface/tally.ledger.undo']
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
- id: C:behaviour/read
  name: Reading the ledger
  summary: A missing ledger is empty; blank lines are skipped; any other line that is not an entry stops the command with its line number.
  does: Reads the file as UTF-8, numbers its lines from 1 (blank lines counted), skips blank ones, and builds one Entry per line.
  when: any command
  errors:
  - {when: 'a line is not a JSON object with at, name and delta', message: 'tally: <path>: line <n> is not a tally entry', exit: 1}
  of: ['C:interface/tally.ledger.read']
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
- id: C:behaviour/show
  name: Show draws bars
  summary: tally show prints one row per name, the name padded, the total right-aligned and a bar of '#' scaled so the largest positive total gets 30.
  does: Names in alphabetical order; a total of 0 is left out unless --all; each row is NAME padded to the longest name, two spaces, TOTAL right-aligned to the widest total, two spaces, the bar, with trailing space removed; a bar is round(total * 30 / largest positive total) characters, at least one for any positive total; a negative total has no bar. --json prints the same totals (0 left out unless --all) as one JSON object with sorted keys.
  when: tally show [--all] [--json]
  edges:
  - given: 'totals {a: 10, bb: 1, c: 0}'
    then: ['a   10  ##############################', 'bb   1  ###']
  - given: 'totals {a: -2}'
    then: [a  -2]
  - {given: no rows to show, then: 'prints empty_message: "nothing tallied yet (or every total is 0; try --all)", or "nothing tallied yet" with --all'}
  of: ['C:interface/command.show', 'C:interface/tally.render.rows']
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
- id: C:behaviour/errors
  name: Errors and exit status
  summary: 'A LedgerError is printed as "tally: <message>" on standard error with exit status 1; a usage error is argparse''s, exit status 2.'
  does: main catches LedgerError only; any other exception is not caught.
  when: any command
  of: ['C:interface/tally.cli.main']
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
they lean on:
- id: C:reliance/whole-numbers-unbounded
  name: whole numbers without limit
  gives: Whole numbers have no fixed width. Adding, subtracting and multiplying them never overflows and never loses a digit, however large they grow.
  example: 18446744073709551615 plus 1 is 18446744073709551616, exactly; a total past two to the sixty-third is kept.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: math/big.Int where a number may pass 64 bits, note: int is 64 bits and wraps silently; every sum that may grow past it is written on big.Int}
- id: C:reliance/number-from-text
  name: a whole number read from text
  gives: A whole number is read from text that may have spaces, tabs or line ends around it, a plus or minus sign, single underscores between digits, leading zeros, and the decimal digits of any script, not only 0 to 9. Anything else is refused.
  example: ''' 5_0'', ''+7'', ''007'' and the Arabic-Indic digit seven are read as 50, 7, 7 and 7; ''5__0'' and ''1.0'' are refused.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: strconv.ParseInt after trimming, note: 'underscores between digits, signs and non-ASCII digits the original accepts are glue to write'}
- id: C:reliance/halves-round-to-even
  name: halves round to the even neighbour
  gives: Rounding a number to a whole number takes the nearer whole number, and a number exactly halfway goes to the even one. The result is a whole number.
  example: 2.5 rounds to 2, 3.5 to 4, and -0.5 to 0.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: math.RoundToEven}
- id: C:reliance/division-gives-fraction
  name: dividing gives a fraction
  gives: Dividing one whole number by another with the plain division sign gives a fractional number, correctly rounded, even when the division is exact.
  example: 6 divided by 3 is 2.0, not 2; 1 divided by 3 is 0.3333333333333333.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: float64 division after converting both sides}
- id: C:reliance/fractions-are-doubles
  name: fractional numbers are binary doubles
  gives: A fractional number is a 64-bit binary floating-point number. Not-a-number is unequal to everything, itself included; there is a positive and a negative zero; a literal too large to hold reads as infinity.
  example: 0.1 plus 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004; 1e400 is infinity.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: float64}
- id: C:reliance/fraction-from-text
  name: a fractional number read from text
  gives: A fractional number is read from text with spaces around it, a sign, underscores between digits, an exponent, and the words nan, inf and infinity in any case.
  example: ''' -1_0.5e1 '' reads as -105.0; ''Infinity'' reads as infinity.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: strconv.ParseFloat after trimming, note: 'the spellings of infinity and not-a-number, and underscores, as the original reads them, are glue'}
- id: C:reliance/number-as-text
  name: numbers written as text
  gives: A whole number is written in decimal digits with a minus sign when negative. A fractional number is written with the fewest digits that read back as the same number, always with a point or an exponent; from 1e16 up and below 1e-4 it takes the exponent form, with a sign and at least two digits.
  example: 1.0 is written 1.0, not 1; 1e16 is written 1e+16; 0.0001 is written 0.0001 and 0.00001 is written 1e-05.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: 'the printed form of a number around strconv.FormatFloat(x, ''g'', -1, 64)', note: 'the shortest digits agree; where the form switches to an exponent, how the exponent is spelled, inf and nan, and the trailing .0 are written'}
- id: C:reliance/conversions
  name: values converted to a kind
  gives: Converting a value to a whole number drops a fraction toward zero and takes yes as 1 and no as 0; converting text reads it as a number (see the entries on numbers read from text); converting anything to text gives its printed form. A value that cannot be converted is refused with a value error or a type error.
  example: a fraction 2.9 converted to a whole number is 2; yes is 1; the text '3' converted is 3; a list is refused.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: 'each conversion the program makes, with the original''s refusals', note: Go converts only where told and fails differently}
- id: C:reliance/text-length-in-code-points
  name: text measured in code points
  gives: The length of a text, and every padding to a width, counts Unicode code points, not bytes, not UTF-16 units and not the columns a terminal draws. A wide character or a combining mark counts as one.
  example: '''café'' is 4 long; padded to 6 it gains two spaces; a name of three CJK ideographs counts 3.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: utf8.RuneCountInString}
- id: C:reliance/text-order-by-code-point
  name: text ordered by code point
  gives: Texts are ordered by comparing code point by code point, not by any language's alphabet and not by locale, so every capital letter of A to Z comes before every small letter, and a shorter text before a longer one it begins.
  example: sorted, 'B', 'a', 'é' and 'b' come out as 'B', 'a', 'b', 'é'.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: string comparison, note: UTF-8 bytes order as their code points do}
- id: C:reliance/sort-is-stable
  name: sorting keeps ties in order
  gives: Sorting is stable. Things that compare equal under the sort's key keep the order they had before.
  example: sorted by length, 'bb', 'a', 'c' give 'a', 'c', 'bb'.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: 'sort.SliceStable, slices.SortStableFunc'}
- id: C:reliance/what-is-a-space
  name: what counts as white space
  gives: White space is every character Unicode's database classes as a space separator or as a bidirectional space, segment or paragraph separator. That is the ASCII space, tab, line feed, vertical tab, form feed and carriage return, the four information separators U+001C to U+001F, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F and U+3000. Trimming, splitting on white space and asking whether a text is white space all use this one set.
  example: a name of 'tea' followed by U+3000 is trimmed to 'tea'; 'a', U+001F, 'b' holds white space.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: unicode.IsSpace with U+001C to U+001F added, note: the set is written out}
- id: C:reliance/lines-end-at
  name: where a line ends
  gives: A text split into lines breaks at line feed, carriage return, carriage return then line feed (one break), line tabulation, form feed, the file, group and record separators U+001C to U+001E, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029. The breaks are not kept, and a final break does not make an empty last line.
  example: '''a'', U+2028, ''b'' is two lines; ''a\r\nb\n'' is two lines, ''a'' and ''b''.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: a line splitter ending lines where the original does, note: 'Go splits only where told; \r\n, \r, \v, \f, U+001C to U+001E, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029 are written'}
- id: C:reliance/text-repeated
  name: text repeated
  gives: A text repeated a whole number of times is that many copies joined; zero or a negative number of times gives the empty text, never an error.
  example: '''#'' three times is ''###''; ''#'' minus two times is ''''.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: strings.Repeat}
- id: C:reliance/printed-form
  name: a value's printed form
  gives: Any value has a printed form. Text prints as itself; bytes print as b followed by the quoted bytes; a quoted form of text (used in many messages) puts it in single quotes, or double quotes when it holds a single quote and no double one, with backslash escapes for what cannot be shown.
  example: the bytes of '<r>' print as b'<r>'; the quoted form of x is 'x', of it's is "it's".
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: 'the original''s printed form of texts, lists and maps', note: fmt's %v and %q print differently}
- id: C:reliance/format-spec
  name: the format of a value written into text
  gives: A value written into text may carry a format of fill, alignment, sign, width, grouping, precision and type. A plus sign shows the sign of positive numbers too; a width pads to that many code points; a fraction's precision rounds half to even.
  example: 1 formatted with a sign is '+1' and -2 is '-2'; 3 right-aligned in width 4 is '   3'.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: 'the format fields the program uses, over fmt.Sprintf', note: 'fmt''s verbs differ in alignment, grouping and rounding'}
- id: C:reliance/truth-of-values
  name: which values count as false
  gives: Where a value is tested as a condition, zero of any kind, empty text, an empty list, map or set, and nothing count as false; everything else counts as true unless it says otherwise.
  example: a line holding only spaces, trimmed, is empty and so false; 0.0 is false; a list holding one empty text is true.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: each test of truth written out, note: 'Go has no truth of values: a test names what it tests'}
- id: C:reliance/any-all-stop-early
  name: any and all stop at the first answer
  gives: Asking whether any of a series holds stops at the first that does; asking whether all hold stops at the first that does not; the rest are never looked at. Any of nothing is false and all of nothing is true.
  example: of handlers checked in order, the second is never examined when the first already answers.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: a loop that returns at the first answer}
- id: C:reliance/map-keeps-order
  name: a map of keys to values
  gives: A map from keys to values holds each key once and keeps the order in which keys were first put in; putting a key in again changes its value and keeps its place; a map built from sorted pairs stays sorted. Looking up a key it does not hold is refused with a key error unless a default is given.
  example: a="1" b="2" a="3" gives a=3 then b=2; the totals of b, a and c, put in sorted, come back a, b, c.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: a slice of keys kept beside the map, note: Go's maps keep no order}
- id: C:reliance/set-members
  name: a set holds each value once
  gives: A set holds each value once, two values that compare equal (and hash alike) being one member; membership is asked in about constant time.
  example: two findings with the same file, line and name are one finding.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: 'map[T]struct{}'}
- id: C:reliance/set-order-varies
  name: the order of a set of texts varies from run to run
  gives: Going through a set of texts visits them in an order that changes from one run of the program to the next, because the hash of a text is salted afresh at each start; only a sort makes it repeatable.
  example: the same three names, put in a set and printed, come out in a different order on another run.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: map iteration, note: its order varies from run to run as well; only a sort makes it repeatable}
- id: C:reliance/membership-identity-then-equality
  name: membership is identity first, then equality
  gives: Asking whether a value is among others asks, for each, whether it is that very object, then whether it is equal; the first yes answers.
  example: a constant compared against a list of constants by membership finds itself even if equality was redefined.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: '== on values, with the identity cases written', note: not-a-number is equal to itself under identity}
- id: C:reliance/lists-and-zip
  name: pairing lists stops at the shortest
  gives: Walking two series in step stops at the end of the shorter one, silently; the largest or smallest of nothing is refused unless a default is given.
  example: pairing 'a', 'b', 'c' with 1, 2 gives two pairs; the largest of no totals with a default of 0 is 0.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: a loop to the shorter length}
- id: C:reliance/error-text
  name: an error printed is its message
  gives: An error turned into text gives its message as it was raised, and the empty text when it was raised with none.
  example: an error raised with 'the ledger is broken' prints as that; one raised with no message prints as nothing.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: err.Error()}
- id: C:reliance/error-kinds
  name: errors caught by kind
  gives: A handler catches the kinds of error it names and every kind made from them. A text that is not valid JSON is a kind of value error; a missing key is a key error; a wrong kind of value is usually a type error; a missing file, a folder where a file was wanted and a refused permission are kinds of operating-system error.
  example: a line that is not JSON and a line missing a field are both caught by one handler naming value and key errors.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: typed errors with errors.Is and errors.As}
- id: C:reliance/chained-errors
  name: an error raised from another
  gives: An error raised while another is handled, or raised from it, keeps the first as its cause; an uncaught one reports both, the cause first.
  example: a decode error turned into a ledger error prints both, when nobody catches the second.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: 'fmt.Errorf with %w, errors.Unwrap', note: the report the original prints of a chain is written}
- id: C:reliance/missing-key-error
  name: a missing key's error names the key
  gives: Looking up a key a map does not hold raises a key error whose text is the key's quoted form.
  example: looking up 'other' among the tree builders fails with the text 'other' in single quotes.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: the message naming the key}
- id: C:reliance/program-arguments
  name: the program's own arguments
  gives: The program's own arguments are the words it was started with, after its name, as text; bytes that are not valid in the locale's encoding are kept as lone surrogates so that they round-trip.
  example: started as 'tool add tea 3', the arguments are 'add', 'tea' and '3'.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: os.Args}
- id: C:reliance/argparse-surface
  name: the option reader's errors and messages
  gives: 'A refused command line prints the usage line, then "PROG: error: MESSAGE", on standard error and exits with status 2. The messages are fixed phrases: "the following arguments are required: X", "unrecognized arguments: A B", "argument X: invalid choice: ''V'' (choose from a, b)" (the choices unquoted, as 3.13.11 was recorded; earlier releases quoted them), "argument X: invalid int value: ''V''", "argument X: ignored explicit argument ''V''", "ambiguous option: --x could match --xa, --xb". Values are shown in their quoted form. A sub-command''s errors name it ("tool add") and print its own usage line; words a sub-command does not take are reported by the top level.'
  example: 'started with no command, it prints "usage: tally [-h] [--version] {add,show,undo} ..." and "tally: error: the following arguments are required: command" and exits 2.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: 'an option reader with the original''s usage line, errors and exit status 2', note: the flag package has none of them, gap: 'the option reader written (a few hundred lines): usage line, error messages, exit status 2'}
- id: C:reliance/argparse-help
  name: the option reader's help screen
  gives: Asking for help prints, on standard output, the usage line, a blank line, the description, then "positional arguments:" and "options:" with each argument's help, indented two spaces, the help column at the longest invocation plus two (capped at 24), wrapped to the terminal's width; "-h, --help" says "show this help message and exit"; then it exits 0.
  example: '"tally -h" ends with "--version  show program''s version number and exit", and exits 0.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: 'the help screen, laid out as the original lays it out'}
- id: C:reliance/argparse-version
  name: the version option
  gives: The version option prints the version text and a line end on standard output and exits 0, as soon as it is met, before any later word is checked.
  example: '"tally --version add" prints "tally 0.2.0" and exits 0; "tally add tea --version" is refused.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: the version option}
- id: C:reliance/argparse-abbreviation
  name: long options may be shortened
  gives: A long option may be given by any prefix that names only one option; a prefix naming several is refused as ambiguous.
  example: '"--vers" is read as "--version"; "--a" as "--all" when no other option begins so.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: 'unambiguous prefixes of long options, in the option reader'}
- id: C:reliance/argparse-negative-numbers
  name: negative numbers are values
  gives: A word that looks like a negative number (minus then digits, with a point allowed) is taken as a value, not an option, while no option looks like one; a word that holds a space is always a value.
  example: '"tally add tea -2" adds -2; "tally add tea -1.5" is refused as an invalid whole number.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: 'a negative number taken as a value, in the option reader'}
- id: C:reliance/argparse-optional-positional
  name: an optional value is matched once
  gives: Values are matched to the arguments a run of plain words at a time; an optional value (zero or one) is matched in the first run even to nothing, so a plain word after an option in between is an unrecognised argument.
  example: '"tally add tea --x 3" reports "unrecognized arguments: --x 3".'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: 'an optional value matched once, in the option reader'}
- id: C:reliance/argparse-subcommands
  name: sub-commands
  gives: A command made of sub-commands takes every word after the sub-command's name for that sub-command; a missing sub-command, when required, is reported as a required argument under its destination's name; an unknown one is an invalid choice; a first "--" ends the options.
  example: '"tally frob" reports "argument command: invalid choice: ''frob'' (choose from add, show, undo)", the choices unquoted.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: 'sub-commands, in the option reader'}
- id: C:reliance/environment-read
  name: the environment read as text
  gives: The environment is a map of names to text, read once when the program starts; a name that is not set is absent, which is told apart from one set to the empty text.
  example: with TALLY_FILE set to the empty text, the variable is present and empty.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: os.LookupEnv}
- id: C:reliance/clock-seconds
  name: the time in seconds
  gives: The time now is a fractional number of seconds since 1970-01-01 at midnight UTC, with as much precision as the system gives (usually below a microsecond).
  example: a moment in November 2026 reads as about 1794000000.123456.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: time.Now() as seconds since the epoch}
- id: C:reliance/terminal-width
  name: the terminal's width
  gives: The width of the terminal is read from the COLUMNS variable, else from the terminal, else taken as 80.
  example: with COLUMNS set to 40, help is wrapped to 40 columns.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: 'COLUMNS, else 80', note: the terminal's own size needs golang.org/x/term; the original's order is COLUMNS first}
- id: C:reliance/print-line-end
  name: printing a line
  gives: Printing writes its values separated by one space and ends with one line feed, on standard output unless another stream is named; the stream is written in order and flushed when the program ends.
  example: 'printing ''tea: 3'' writes ''tea: 3'' and a line feed; an error printed to the error stream goes there.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: fmt.Println}
- id: C:reliance/output-encoding
  name: the encoding of printed text
  gives: Printed text is encoded as UTF-8 on macOS and wherever the locale asks for UTF-8 or is the plain C locale; elsewhere in the locale's encoding, where a character that cannot be encoded stops the program with an error.
  example: a name with an ñ prints as UTF-8 bytes even with LANG=C.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: UTF-8 bytes written as they are}
- id: C:reliance/json-written
  name: JSON as written
  gives: 'JSON is written on one line with ", " between items and ": " after keys; every character outside ASCII is written as a backslash, u and four lowercase hex digits (a pair of them for a character beyond U+FFFF), and control characters likewise, except the short escapes for quote, backslash, line feed, carriage return, tab, backspace and form feed; numbers are written as in the entry on numbers written as text; not-a-number and the infinities are written NaN, Infinity and -Infinity.'
  example: 'a name "café" with 3 is written {"café" written as "café": 3}; a time 1.5 is written 1.5.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: 'a JSON writer with the original''s spacing, escapes and number forms', note: 'encoding/json escapes <, > and &, writes no spaces and spells numbers its own way'}
- id: C:reliance/json-keys-sorted
  name: JSON keys sorted
  gives: Asked to sort keys, JSON is written with each object's keys in code-point order.
  example: '{"name": "tea", "at": 1.0, "delta": 3} is written {"at": 1.0, "delta": 3, "name": "tea"}.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: encoding/json sorts a map's keys}
- id: C:reliance/json-read
  name: JSON as read
  gives: JSON is read with white space (space, tab, line feed, carriage return) allowed around values; a number without a fraction or an exponent becomes a whole number of any size, exactly, any other a fractional number; NaN, Infinity and -Infinity are accepted; a raw control character inside a string is refused; a key given twice keeps its last value; anything else is refused with a decoding error, a kind of value error.
  example: '{"delta": 99999999999999999999} reads the delta exactly; {"a": 1, "a": 2} reads a = 2; {"at": NaN} is read.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: encoding/json with a Decoder and UseNumber, note: 'the original reads NaN and Infinity and numbers of any size: glue where the program meets them'}
- id: C:reliance/home-and-tilde
  name: the home folder and ~
  gives: The home folder is the HOME variable when it is set, else the account's entry in the system's password database. A path beginning with ~ has it replaced by the home folder (a trailing slash of the home dropped), and ~user by that account's home; a user the system does not know is refused with an error saying the home folder could not be determined.
  example: with HOME=/home/ann, '~/x' is '/home/ann/x'; '~nobody-here/x' is refused.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: os.UserHomeDir, note: a leading ~ is expanded by a line of glue}
- id: C:reliance/path-written
  name: paths written the POSIX way
  gives: A path is written as text with its parts joined by '/', '.' parts and repeated slashes dropped, no trailing slash, a leading '//' kept, '..' left as it is, and '.' for an empty path; a relative path stays relative.
  example: '''./a//b/'' is written ''a/b''; '''' is written ''.''.'
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: path/filepath}
- id: C:reliance/path-kinds
  name: what a path names
  gives: A path names a file, a folder, something else, or nothing; a broken link names nothing, so asking whether it exists says no; a path under a file names nothing too.
  example: a broken link named on the command line is reported as not found.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: 'os.Stat, os.Lstat'}
- id: C:reliance/make-folders
  name: folders made as needed
  gives: Making a folder with its parents makes every missing folder on the way; asked not to mind one that exists, it says nothing when the folder is there, but is still refused when a file stands where a folder should.
  example: a ledger at ~/a/b/x.jsonl makes ~/a and ~/a/b first; a file named ~/a makes it fail.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: os.MkdirAll}
- id: C:reliance/file-created-mode
  name: the permissions of a new file
  gives: A file the program creates gets read and write permission for everyone (0666) less the user's mask, and a new folder 0777 less the mask.
  example: with a mask of 022, a new ledger is 0644 and a new folder 0755.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: 'os.OpenFile with 0o666, the umask applied'}
- id: C:reliance/newlines-translated
  name: line ends read and written as text
  gives: A file read as text turns carriage return and line feed, and a lone carriage return, into a line feed; written as text, a line feed is written as it is on macOS and Linux and as carriage return and line feed on Windows.
  example: a file holding 'a\r\nb' is read as 'a\nb'.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: written, what: \r\n and \r read as \n where the original reads text, note: Go translates no line ends}
- id: C:reliance/text-decoding-strict
  name: text decoded strictly
  gives: Text decoded as UTF-8 refuses the first byte sequence that is not valid UTF-8 with a decoding error, a kind of value error, naming the position; a byte-order mark at the start is kept as the character U+FEFF, unless the encoding asked for is the one that drops it.
  example: a ledger holding the byte 0xE9 alone fails to read; a file beginning with a byte-order mark gives a first line that begins with U+FEFF.
  ruling:
  - {is: kept, said: as proposed}
  provided: {by: built-in, what: utf8.Valid, note: the error the original raises is written}

the cases, which are the judge:
- id: P:case/add-and-totals
  name: Adds fold into totals
  of: ['C:interface/tally.ledger.add', 'C:interface/tally.ledger.totals']
  given:
    calls: ['add(p, "tea", now=1.0)', 'add(p, "tea", 2, now=2.0)', 'add(p, "walks", now=3.0)']
  expect: {value: 'totals(read(p)) == {"tea": 3, "walks": 1}'}
- id: P:case/bad-names-and-zero
  name: Bad names and zero are refused
  of: ['C:interface/tally.ledger.add']
  given:
    calls: ['add(p, "two words")', 'add(p, "tea", 0)']
  expect:
    raises: [LedgerError matching "one word", LedgerError matching "changes nothing"]
    files: the ledger does not exist
- id: P:case/rows
  name: Rows scale bars and hide 0
  of: ['C:interface/tally.render.rows']
  given:
    calls: ['rows({"a": 10, "bb": 1, "c": 0})', 'rows({"a": -2})', 'rows({"c": 0})', 'rows({"c": 0}, show_all=True)']
  expect:
    value: ['["a   10  " + 30 marks, "bb   1  ###"]', '["a  -2"]', '[]', '["c  0"]']
- id: P:case/cli-json-and-error
  name: The command line's JSON and its error exit
  of: ['C:interface/tally.cli.main', 'C:behaviour/errors']
  given:
    env: TALLY_FILE=<a fresh file>
    arguments: [add tea 3, show --json, add "two words"]
  expect:
    exit: [0, 0, 1]
    output: '{"tea": 3}'
    error-output: 'tally: a name is one word, with no spaces'

# tally in Go: the layout

A layout of tally.fabulac.cosm for its transconception into Go: the files of the program to be, in the order they are written, what each holds, and the name each kept interface takes there. Written from the fabulac alone.

## Files, in the order they are written

| # | file | holds |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | go.mod | the Go package |
| 2 | main.go | the whole program |

## Interfaces

| interface | file | name |
|---|---|---|
| C:interface/command.tally | main.go | N_command_tally |
| C:interface/command.add | main.go | N_command_add |
| C:interface/command.show | main.go | N_command_show |
| C:interface/command.undo | main.go | N_command_undo |
| C:interface/tally.cli.main | main.go | N_tally_cli_main |
| C:interface/tally.ledger.ledger_path | main.go | N_tally_ledger_ledger_path |
| C:interface/tally.ledger.read | main.go | N_tally_ledger_read |
| C:interface/tally.ledger.add | main.go | N_tally_ledger_add |
| C:interface/tally.ledger.undo | main.go | N_tally_ledger_undo |
| C:interface/tally.ledger.totals | main.go | N_tally_ledger_totals |
| C:interface/tally.ledger.LedgerError | main.go | N_tally_ledger_LedgerError |
| C:interface/tally.render.rows | main.go | N_tally_render_rows |
| C:interface/tally.render.empty_message | main.go | N_tally_render_empty_message |
| C:interface/format.ledger-line | main.go | N_format_ledger_line |

| gap | fill |
